findings.text: totalAssets() values the strategy's getBalances() LP amounts, which are taken at the pool's spot price, using a TWAP tick, or the spot slot0 tick when twapWindowSeconds==0 or observe() reverts; an attacker can flash-swap the pool to push the spot price away from the TWAP, which inflates the reported LP value, redeem shares at the inflated convertToAssets() rate (the share-ratio slippage mins are computed from the same manipulated balances, so they pass), then swap back, taking the difference from the remaining shareholders.

When twapWindowSeconds is 0, or observe() reverts and the code falls back to slot0, convertToShares() is priced off the manipulable spot tick; an attacker can move the pool price in one transaction to lower the value of the vault's non-asset holdings, deposit (or depositWithReferral) to mint extra shares cheaply, restore the price, and redeem to dilute and drain existing depositors.
